scope: Physics, vehicle control, simulator fidelity and calibration; research only

sources.title: Control of Complex Maneuvers for a Quadrotor UAV using Geometric Methods on SE(3)
sources.organization: Taeyoung Lee; Melvin Leok; N. Harris McClamroch / arXiv
sources.claim: Equations (2)-(5) give SE(3) rigid-body dynamics; (8)-(11) define rotation/rate errors and a feed-forward geometric moment law. Proposition 1 imposes attitude-error and initial rate bounds.
sources.limitations: The paper directly controls thrust and moments and does not supply a proof for AeroMesh's nonnegative bounded rotor thrusts, mixer saturation, thrust lag, PI velocity loop, or rate clamps. Its gravity and thrust signs differ from AeroMesh's Z-up/+body-Z convention. Numerical demonstrations are not airframe qualification.
sources.access: Full native HTML read; TeX alttext preserved. Jina full-text proxy redirected incorrectly and was not used for equations.

sources.title: Differential Flatness of Quadrotor Dynamics Subject to Rotor Drag for Accurate Tracking of High-Speed Trajectories
sources.organization: Matthias Faessler; Antonio Franchi; Davide Scaramuzza / University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, LAAS-CNRS
sources.claim: Equations (1)-(5) model mass-normalized body-axis linear rotor drag and a speed-dependent thrust correction; Section III explicitly assumes no wind, stiff propellers, and no rotor-drag dependence on thrust.
sources.limitations: Flatness is derived for this lumped model and smooth trajectories; it is not a result for arbitrary turbulence, stalls, contact, or actuator saturation. The constant D has units 1/s, whereas AeroMesh force-drag constants are N/(m/s).
sources.access: Full native HTML read; TeX alttext preserved.

sources.title: GymPyBulletDrones BaseAviary physics, ground effect, drag, and downwash models
sources.organization: Learning Systems and Robotics Lab / GymPyBulletDrones contributors
sources.claim: Base model uses force=KF*RPM^2 and reaction torque=KM*RPM^2; optional ground effect scales with squared rotor-radius/height ratio, drag scales with summed rotor angular speed, and downwash uses a fitted vertical Gaussian footprint.
sources.limitations: Code includes empirical coefficients and guards; these are not universal aerodynamic constants. The current repository differs from the IROS 2021 paper branch. Downwash is applied in LINK_FRAME and only to lower nearby vehicles, a material frame/model detail to test before reuse.
sources.access: Official GitHub API source and README read; repository redirects from utiasDSL to learnsyslab.

sources.title: RotorS Gazebo motor model
sources.organization: ETH Zurich Autonomous Systems Lab / RotorS contributors
sources.claim: Motor plugin uses squared real angular speed for thrust, rotor-axis-perpendicular relative wind for linear rotor drag, reaction torque proportional to thrust, and a motor-speed filter. It explicitly warns about visual joint angular-speed aliasing.
sources.limitations: This is the RotorS Gazebo plugin, not a claim that all Gazebo models include it. Parameters require rotor/airframe identification. Joint-speed slowdown and aerodynamic motor speed are distinct.
sources.access: Official GitHub API source read.

sources.title: Bullet btDiscreteDynamicsWorld::stepSimulation
sources.organization: Bullet Physics contributors
sources.claim: stepSimulation accumulates time for fixed substeps, caps executed substeps, clears accumulated forces after stepping, and takes a single variable step when maxSubSteps=0. Contact solving and collision detection occur within internal steps.
sources.limitations: The inspected upstream commit is not asserted to be the exact Bullet build bundled in Panda3D 1.10.16. Small fixed steps improve numerical resolution but do not calibrate aerodynamics or guarantee continuous collision avoidance.
sources.access: Official GitHub API source read.

sources.title: Panda3D 1.10: Bullet Hello World
sources.organization: Panda3D documentation project
sources.claim: Official guide recommends SI units, distinguishes positive-mass dynamic bodies from zero-mass static bodies, and documents doPhysics(dt,maxSubsteps,stepsize), with a smaller-step/performance tradeoff.
sources.limitations: Introductory engine documentation is not an aviation accuracy benchmark. The attempted /rigid-bodies URL was a 404 and is not evidence.
sources.access: Official panda3d-docs 1.10 source programming/physics/bullet/hello-world.rst read through GitHub API.

sources.title: Panda3D 1.10: Bullet Continuous Collision Detection
sources.organization: Panda3D documentation project
sources.claim: CCD addresses between-frame tunneling by sweeping a configured sphere rather than the complete body shape, enabled with a motion threshold and swept-sphere radius.
sources.limitations: CCD does not imply accurate propeller/frame impact geometry, crash survival, or safe separation. AeroMesh's 0.28 m swept radius is smaller than its 0.35 m body sphere, so exact collision envelopes still need dedicated fixtures.
sources.access: Official panda3d-docs 1.10 source programming/physics/bullet/ccd.rst read through GitHub API.

sources.title: PX4 rate control implementation
sources.organization: PX4 Autopilot contributors
sources.claim: Rate controller combines proportional error, integral, measured angular-acceleration derivative, and rate-setpoint feed-forward. Integrator growth is blocked in the direction of allocation saturation and bounded.
sources.limitations: This is upstream PX4 source, not the controller currently running in AeroMesh. PX4 tuning values and normalized torque output cannot be copied directly into SI torque gains.
sources.access: Official GitHub API source read.

sources.title: Using PX4's Navigation Filter (EKF2)
sources.organization: PX4 documentation project
sources.claim: EKF2 buffers sensors on a delayed fusion horizon, compensates configured delays, and propagates estimates to current time with buffered IMU data; IMU/body lever arms and separate sensor-fault modes matter.
sources.limitations: This current main documentation is not evidence that the AeroMesh engine or ProjectAirSim client runs EKF2. Ground-truth observations lack these effects. Delay/noise settings require measured sensor data.
sources.access: Official documentation read through Jina text route.

sources.title: PX4 Controller Diagrams
sources.organization: PX4 documentation project
sources.claim: Official diagrams describe cascaded multicopter position/velocity/attitude/rate loops, saturation and anti-windup, gyro filtering, and normalized thrust/torque interfaces.
sources.limitations: Main documentation evolves. Similar loop topology is not equivalence to AeroMesh control gains, motor dynamics, filters, or validated hardware behavior. The PX4 parameter prefix MPC denotes multicopter position control, not necessarily model predictive control.
sources.access: Official documentation read through Jina text route.

sources.title: Kalibr IMU Noise Model
sources.organization: ETH Zurich Autonomous Systems Lab / Kalibr contributors
sources.claim: White-noise sample standard deviation is density/sqrt(dt) with the stated ideal filtering assumption; random-walk bias increments scale as density*sqrt(dt). Static Allan-deviation fitting is described.
sources.limitations: The source explicitly warns that direct subsampling does not justify the same scaling and that static constant-temperature calibration omits motion, scale-factor, and temperature effects. Independent Gaussian axes are a simplifying model.
sources.access: Official raw GitHub wiki Markdown read after the Jina route returned no useful body.

sources.title: Gazebo Sim 9 WindEffects Class Reference
sources.organization: Gazebo / Open Robotics
sources.claim: The documented plugin is a uniform-world wind model with filtered/noisy horizontal magnitude/direction and vertical amplitude; link forces are approximate functions of link mass and relative wind velocity with optional spatial scaling.
sources.limitations: This is not urban CFD, resolved wakes, Dryden/von Karman turbulence, or calibrated rotor aerodynamics merely because it has a wind plugin. Features depend on the selected SDF/plugins.
sources.access: Official API documentation read through Jina text route.

sources.title: ProjectAirSim Fast Physics for Drones
sources.organization: IAMAI ProjectAirSim / Microsoft and IAMAI contributors
sources.claim: Fast Physics uses rigid-body motion with a cuboid body, rotors treated as point masses, cuboid/cylindrical drag faces, and simple responses to Unreal collision detections.
sources.limitations: This inspected upstream source snapshot is not asserted to match the exact locally installed v1.0.1 binary. Rendering detail does not establish aerodynamic or impact validity.
sources.access: Official GitHub API Markdown and corresponding physics source inspected.

sources.title: ProjectAirSim Battery sensor
sources.organization: IAMAI ProjectAirSim / Microsoft and IAMAI contributors
sources.claim: The source explicitly describes mission-planning battery estimation rather than battery modeling; options include configurable drain and simplified rotor torque-times-angular-speed energy drain.
sources.limitations: The example's comment '1 Amp hour = 3600 * Joules' is dimensionally incorrect: Ah is charge (3600 C), and joules require voltage integration. Do not copy that conversion. Neither mode is an equivalent-circuit cell/temperature/charging model.
sources.access: Official GitHub API Markdown read.

sources.title: Physics Sub-Stepping in Unreal Engine
sources.organization: Epic Games
sources.claim: Substepping trades CPU/memory cost for smaller physics intervals; forces are maintained across substeps and collision callbacks can be delayed/queued until the final substep.
sources.limitations: The retrieved page is labeled Unreal Engine 5.8 and contains legacy APEX/mobile notes. Its generic scheduling guidance does not establish exact behavior of the paused local engine version or a ProjectAirSim external physics provider.
sources.confidence: high for documented scheduling; medium for version-specific applicability
sources.access: Official documentation read through Jina text route.

sources.title: Energy Minimization for Wireless Communication with Rotary-Wing UAV
sources.organization: Yong Zeng; Jie Xu; Rui Zhang / National University of Singapore and Guangdong University of Technology
sources.claim: Equation (6) combines blade-profile, induced, and parasite power; Section II-B explicitly neglects extra acceleration energy, distinguishes minimum-power endurance speed from minimum-energy-per-distance range speed, and integrates power over time.
sources.limitations: Constant-altitude communications study with numerical optimization results, not a calibrated model of the 1.5 kg AeroMesh airframe. The commonly reused curve omits maneuver energy and should not predict aggressive launch, braking, gust, and landing without extension and identification.
sources.access: Native full HTML read, including Section II-B.

sources.title: Control Barrier Functions for Sampled-Data Systems with Input Delays
sources.organization: Andrew Singletary; Yuxiao Chen; Aaron D. Ames / California Institute of Technology
sources.claim: Provides a backup-controller CBF construction for zero-order-hold systems, reachable-set constraints over an entire sample interval, state-uncertainty treatment using incremental stability, and a known-input-delay extension.
sources.limitations: Requires stated control-affine/Lipschitz and invariant-set assumptions; it is not a guarantee for AeroMesh's velocity projection or unknown jitter. The demonstration is a simulated Segway, not a quadrotor fleet. Sampling only endpoints is insufficient.
sources.access: Native full HTML read through Section III; publication identity checked against Crossref.

sources.title: JSBSim FGWinds turbulence implementation
sources.organization: JSBSim team
sources.claim: MIL-F-8785C/MIL-STD-1797A and Tustin options use altitude-dependent scales, disturbance strengths, and time constants L/V. Source cites Yeager 1998 and explicitly avoids feeding generated turbulence back into airspeed coefficients.
sources.limitations: Model contains imperial-unit assumptions, minimum-height clipping, a default wingspan, and disables these turbulence outputs when V=0. Direct reuse for a hovering multirotor or urban wakes is unjustified without a different advection/hover treatment and validation.
sources.access: Official GitHub API source read.

sources.title: Propeller Thrust
sources.organization: NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.claim: Actuator-disk momentum theory relates thrust to mass flow and velocity jump, with disk velocity equal to the mean of upstream and downstream speeds; the source explicitly excludes practical losses.
sources.limitations: Ideal preliminary model, not blade-element/momentum theory with calibrated losses, multirotor interference, transient descent, ground effect, or tip Mach effects.
sources.access: Official NASA page read through Jina text route.

sources.title: PAMPC: Perception-Aware Model Predictive Control for Quadrotors
sources.organization: Davide Falanga; Philipp Foehn; Peng Lu; Davide Scaramuzza / University of Zurich and ETH Zurich
sources.claim: MPC couples motion and camera objectives with explicit bounds; paper defines mass-normalized thrust. Reported 2 s horizon, 0.1 s transcription steps, 100 Hz update, mean 3.53 ms compute on its Snapdragon Flight ARM platform.
sources.limitations: Perception terms are costs rather than hard visibility constraints. Published single-vehicle hardware timings are not 30-vehicle CPU/RTX3050 performance. Reduced thrust/body-rate plant requires a tracking inner controller; real rotor saturation/lag and contact are not automatically represented.
sources.access: Native full HTML and official rpg_mpc code read.
sources.code_note: The model uses thrust directly as acceleration although sample comments label its bounds N; the paper's mass-normalized definition is authoritative for dimensions.

sources.title: Learning to Fly—a Gym Environment with PyBullet Physics for Reinforcement Learning of Multi-agent Quadcopter Control
sources.organization: Jacopo Panerati; Hehui Zheng; SiQi Zhou; James Xu; Amanda Prorok; Angela P. Schoellig / University of Toronto and University of Cambridge
sources.claim: Provides experimental parameter fitting for Crazyflie ground effect/downwash and reports simulation throughput at specified platform/configuration conditions; explicitly acknowledges incomplete pitch/lateral response in its simplified downwash model.
sources.limitations: Crazyflie coefficients do not transfer to a 1.5 kg/0.28 m-arm vehicle. The 2021 code branch and benchmark machines differ from the current repository and this Windows host. Bullet contacts do not imply complete aerodynamics.
sources.access: Native full HTML read, including model/benchmark limitations.

sources.title: Neural Lander: Stable Drone Landing Control Using Learned Dynamics
sources.organization: Guanya Shi; Xichen Shi; Michael O'Connell; Rose Yu; Kamyar Azizzadenesheli; Animashree Anandkumar; Yisong Yue; Soon-Jo Chung / Caltech and collaborators
sources.claim: Learns a residual near-ground aerodynamic force with spectral normalization and develops stability analysis with bounded learning error; experiments include landing and cross-table motion.
sources.limitations: A bounded Lipschitz network is not itself evidence of a globally bounded residual error on unseen buildings, rotor configurations, or payloads. Ground-effect steady-flow formulas and learned models need task-specific data and uncertainty limits.
sources.access: Native full HTML abstract, problem statement, and stated analysis assumptions read; deeper theorem review continues.

sources.title: Flightmare: A Flexible Quadrotor Simulator
sources.organization: Yunlong Song; Selim Naji; Elia Kaufmann; Antonio Loquercio; Davide Scaramuzza / University of Zurich and ETH Zurich
sources.claim: Separates Unity rendering from selectable physics and reports high throughput for its C++ dynamics and camera rendering under documented scenes/hardware; implements Euler and RK4 integration.
sources.limitations: Up to 200000 dynamics steps/s and 230 rendered frames/s are distinct metrics/configurations. Historical comparisons to AirSim/Gazebo do not describe current IAMAI ProjectAirSim. This is not a benchmark of AeroMesh contacts, swarm planning, radio transport, or 30 cameras.
sources.access: Native full HTML read, with benchmark details extracted.

sources.title: NASA ProgPy BatteryCircuit equivalent-circuit model
sources.organization: NASA Prognostics team
sources.claim: Models current input, charge states in RC components, battery temperature, terminal voltage, and end-of-discharge events; source names a 2013 model-based prognostics reference.
sources.limitations: Example cell/thermal parameters are not an AeroMesh pack calibration. Source says this circuit model is faster and less accurate than its electrochemical alternative. Model validity does not extend to thermal runaway or charger qualification.
sources.access: Official GitHub API source read.

sources.title: Selecting the right charge-management solution
sources.organization: Masoud Beheshti / Texas Instruments
sources.claim: Manufacturer application note describes Li-ion/Li-polymer qualification/preconditioning, constant-current then constant-voltage charge, tapering current, and voltage/temperature-based termination requirements.
sources.limitations: Historical generic application note, not a specification for a selected modern cell or pack; example 4.2 V/cell, current, and termination values must not be assumed for arbitrary chemistries. This report uses only the phase/measurement logic.
sources.access: Primary PDF text read through Jina; source is five pages. No battery hardware actions performed.

sources.title: Panda3D 1.10.16 BulletRigidBodyNode implementation
sources.organization: Panda3D contributors
sources.claim: apply_force passes force and relative position directly to Bullet; set_inertia overrides diagonal local inertia but later mass, shape, or body-scale changes can overwrite it. Current AeroMesh construction sets shape and mass before its explicit inertia.
sources.limitations: This verifies API semantics from a matching Panda3D source tag, not measured physical inertia or every transitive native-library build. Root/body transforms must stay consistent with world-force assumptions.
sources.access: Official GitHub API source read.

sources.title: NASA-STD-7009B: Standard for Models and Simulations
sources.organization: NASA Office of the Chief Engineer
sources.claim: Sections 4.2.3-4.2.7 distinguish implementation/solution verification from conceptual/empirical validation and call for recorded domains, numerical error, assumptions, validation data, and uncertainty appropriate to intended use.
sources.limitations: A methodological reference, not a claim of NASA endorsement, compliance, or certification for this repository. The publication's organizational approval process is not a new approval requirement for this research.
sources.access: Official standard PDF text read through Jina, including verification/validation sections; canonical PDF link discovered from NASA page.

sources.title: Implementation and Testing of Turbulence Models for the F18-HARV Simulation
sources.organization: Jessie C. Yeager / Lockheed Martin Engineering and Sciences for NASA Langley
sources.claim: NASA CR-1998-206937 compares continuous, Tustin and military-standard Dryden implementations using time histories, power spectral density, theoretical/measured statistics, and autocorrelation; statistical studies used ten seeds and 1000 s sequences.
sources.limitations: An F18 fixed-wing simulation reference, not proof of low-speed quadrotor or building-wake validity. PDF OCR distorts equations, so this report uses its verification methodology and the inspectable JSBSim code rather than copying OCR formulas.
sources.confidence: high for metadata/methodology; formula transcription not relied on
sources.access: Official NTRS record and PDF text read through Jina.

sources.title: Bullet 2.84 rigid-body gyroscopic defaults and implicit integration
sources.organization: Bullet Physics contributors
sources.claim: setupRigidBody sets BT_ENABLE_GYROSCOPIC_FORCE_IMPLICIT_BODY; computeGyroscopicImpulseImplicit_Body implements the implicit-body gyroscopic update. Installed Panda3D get_bullet_version() returned 284, and a nonprincipal-axis numerical probe observes the expected coupling with timestep-dependent damping.
sources.limitations: The reported native library version matches this release tag; this is not a complete native-build provenance audit. The ideal compensation probe directly injects torque and does not validate the allocated motor path or physical inertia.
sources.access: Matching official raw source read; installed native version and isolated numerical behavior recorded in physics-rotation-20261106-01.json.

sources.title: RotorPy: A Python-based Multirotor Simulator with Aerodynamics for Education and Research
sources.organization: Spencer Folk; James Paulos; Vijay Kumar / University of Pennsylvania
sources.claim: The paper models body-axis quadratic parasitic drag, rotor-speed-dependent linear drag and blade-flapping moment, first-order rotor-speed dynamics, and sensors. Current code documents ignored frame lift/moment effects and wind assumed approximately uniform over one vehicle; simulate.py terminates on unsafe/collision conditions rather than resolving Bullet-like impacts.
sources.limitations: Aerodynamic coefficients require identification. The current v3 repository is newer than the 2023 paper; its feature-projection cameras are not a photorealistic renderer. Batched CPU/GPU claims are not measurements for this 30-drone Windows mission or RTX 3050.
sources.access: Full native paper HTML and official pinned README, vehicle documentation, and simulation source read.

sources.title: Crazyflow: An Accurate, GPU-Accelerated, Differentiable Drone Simulator in JAX
sources.organization: Martin Schuck; Marcel P. Rath; Yufei Hua; Abhishek Goudar; SiQi Zhou; Angela P. Schoellig / Learning Systems and Robotics Lab
sources.claim: JAX owns batched analytical/abstracted drone dynamics. Official MuJoCo integration documentation marks drone geometries as kinematic mocap bodies, synchronizes them only for rendering/contact queries, and states added geometry has no effect on drone dynamics. Benchmarks use Ryzen 9 7950X and RTX 4090 and become GPU-favorable at larger independent-world batches.
sources.limitations: Contact detection is not contact response in this integration. The 914M-step/s headline uses 262144 independent worlds with one drone each, not 30 interacting drones in one mission. README requires Python 3.11+ and its GPU extra targets Linux x86-64/CUDA 12, unlike the current Windows/Python 3.10 environment. No local installation or performance measurement occurred.
sources.access: Native paper HTML and official pinned README/MuJoCo integration documentation read.

sources.title: UIUC Propeller Database, Volumes 1–4
sources.organization: John B. Brandt; Robert W. Deters; Gavin K. Ananda; Or D. Dantsker; Michael S. Selig / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
sources.claim: Wind-tunnel measurements provide thrust and torque for small-UAV propellers. Official coefficient image defines advance ratio J=V/(nD), CT=T/(rho*n²*D⁴), CP=P/(rho*n³*D⁵), CQ=Q/(rho*n²*D⁵), CP=2*pi*CQ and propulsive efficiency eta=TV/P, with n in revolutions/s. Static Reynolds number uses chord and rotational speed at 75% radius.
sources.limitations: Data apply to specified propellers/test conditions. Rotor thrust, mechanical shaft power, electrical input power, and complete-vehicle power must remain separate. Propulsive efficiency TV/P is zero in static hover and is not hover figure of merit. No database archive or airframe parameters were imported.
sources.access: Official page text read and 9.7 kB basic-equations image downloaded and visually inspected; complete dataset archive not downloaded.
